problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,z,\,y⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the paraboloid $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ and the hemisphere $z=\sqrt{5-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨1,\,0,\,-x⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the paraboloid $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ and the plane $z=1+x.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=1+x$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper plane ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1+x)=1 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(1+x)=0\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=1,\,Q=0,\,R=-x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1\cdot 1-0\cdot 0+(-x))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1-x)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider lower paraboloid ${S}_{2}.$ 

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2x \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=1,\,Q=0,\,R=-x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & =-{∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-1\cdot 2x-0\cdot 2y+(-x))\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-2x-x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1-x)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}3x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x-1\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
